sections.heading: Biography
sections.content: Sam Ananias Cases is a Computer-focused Industrial Technology graduate based in Cebu, Philippines. He focuses on software engineering fundamentals, structured problem decomposition, web standards, and leveraging AI responsibly as an interactive development partner.

sections.heading: Philosophy
sections.content: I believe in building software thoughtfully—thinking through requirements before implementation, documenting key decisions for future context, evaluating trade-offs, and verifying every build through test suites.

facts.label: Education
facts.value: Bachelor of Industrial Technology · Computer major, CTU Danao

facts.label: Current focus
facts.value: Maintainable web development, accessible interfaces, documented decisions

moves.heading: The opening position
moves.lead: A recent graduate treating engineering as a craft to be studied, not a label to be claimed.
body: I am a Computer-focused Industrial Technology graduate based in Cebu, Philippines. My days are split between reading specs, writing small systems end-to-end, and documenting the reasoning behind each structural decision.

This portfolio is my evidence of practice: a public record of what I built, how I built it, and what I am still learning. The goal is not to appear as a finished engineer, but to make the discipline I apply to my work impossible to mistake.

moves.heading: First formal moves in industry
moves.lead: An internship that taught me how production systems behave under real constraints.
body: At Avega Bros. Integrated Shipping Corp in Tayud, Consolacion, I helped ship the BITS biometric timekeeping system, a fleet inventory process, and a CCTV network deployment across multiple sites.

The work was unglamorous and real: cabling, firmware, schema decisions at 02:00, and the quiet discipline of writing down what was decided and why. It is the first time I saw a system I helped build run unattended in front of actual users.

moves.heading: Foundation years
body: My route into software was not linear. I began in hardware — biometric terminals, network switches, the physical layer most developers never touch — before moving into web development, markup, and the discipline of structuring information.

Working across both layers taught me to respect the full system. A web application that cannot survive an actual user's network or a real printer's quirks is software that has not been thought through.

moves.heading: Active repertoire
moves.lead: Four openings I return to, again and again.
body: Web standards and static rendering. Long-lived, readable files beat clever abstractions. Astro, semantic HTML, and CSS-first design systems are my default tools.
Software architecture. I spend more time on the specification than the implementation. A plan that survives five revisions is worth more than ten fast commits.
Automated verification. Tests, accessibility audits, and build checks are not chores; they are how I sleep at night before handing anything over.

AI-paired workflows. I use large language models as serious development partners — for decomposition, edge-case hunting, and critique — while keeping architectural ownership and final review on my desk.

moves.heading: The current position
moves.lead: Deliberate, honest, and slow where it matters.
body: I write before I code. I prefer explicit trade-offs to confident guesses. When AI accelerates me, I document its role plainly. When a decision costs me time today, I expect it to save me more tomorrow.
I am comfortable saying what I do not know. The fastest way to lose trust in a portfolio is to claim depth I have not earned, so I do not.

moves.heading: The endgame letter
moves.lead: What I am building toward, and where to find me.
body: I am working toward a career where the systems I build are quiet, documented, and trustworthy — software that someone can inherit without dreading the discovery process.

If any of this resonates — whether you are evaluating me for a role, considering collaboration, or just want to talk through an engineering decision — the door is open. Email is the most direct way to reach me.
